title: Offhours fidelity & drift pad
body:
Notes-to-self (late shift)

Quick context:
- Running spot checks on two workloads after the 2024-11-01 runtime tweak (kernel prefetch + batch timeout reduction).
- Models: rw-13b-v2 (fp16), rw-70b-q4 (quantized). Small sample size (n~30 each) — exploratory, not a formal sweep.

Observed patterns (high level):
- Slight uptick in short-hallucinations for rw-13b-v2 on factual-extraction tasks (answers inventing verbs/dates). Not huge but consistent across 7/30 samples.
- rw-70b-q4 shows increased trailing-token repetition on long completions when batch timeout hits (likely KV-cache flush timing interacting with timeout).
- Overall latency improved median ~8% but p95 improvement is smaller, and a few samples spike >2x due to fallback routings.

Ad-hoc rubric (quick, 0-3 scale):
- Correctness: 0 (wrong), 1 (partially), 2 (mostly), 3 (clean)
- Verbosity: 0 (under), 1 (bare), 2 (good), 3 (verbose/excess)
- Hallucination severity: 0 (major), 1 (minor factual), 2 (none)
- Degradation trigger: note whether observed when batching >X or timeout triggered

Sample table (raw notes):
- S1 | prompt: "List milestones for Apollo 11" | model: rw-13b-v2 | out: invented "Launch Command Center, July 20, 1969" | score: correctness=1, halluc=1 | note: inserts plausible but wrong label/date for launch site. repeat 3 samples.
- S8 | prompt: legal contract clause extraction (bullet points) | model rw-13b-v2 | out: misses "indemnity" clause, fabricates "breach escalation" paragraph | score: correctness=0, verbosity=2 | note: truncated attention to legal terms.
- S14 | prompt: long creative story (~900 tokens) | rw-70b-q4 | out: mid-story repeats "He looked away" looped x4 at token 420 after batch flush | score: correctness=2, halluc=2, degradation_trigger=batch-timeout=150ms | note: likely kv-cache mis-sync when timeout triggers fallback.

Hypotheses (quick):
1) Kernel prefetch reduced per-token throughput in some small-seq scenarios -> model resorts to attention fallback path that slightly distorts attention distribution -> hallucination risk increased on tight factual extractions.
2) Batch-timeout shortening (150ms) causes more frequent partial batches + KV flushes on rw-70b-q4 quantized path -> repetition bug triggered when KV window misapplied.
3) Fallback routing to compatibility-quantized variant on high-load causes inconsistent behavior across near-identical requests.

Immediate action items:
- Replicate S1+S8 with deterministic seeds (increase to n=200) on rw-13b-v2 with/without kernel-prefetch to isolate. Tag results and open a bug if delta >5% in incorrect answers. (owner: me)
- Add a microtest for KV-cache integrity across batch-timeout boundaries using synthetic long completions (owner: infra, assign to @Leo).
- Instrument trace to log "batch_timeout_event" and "kv_flush" with sample IDs for a 24h window on Canary.

Questions / unresolved:
- Is there a known interaction between prefetch heuristics and attention kernel selection for trimmable layers? (asked infra slack 11/02, no reply yet).
- Should we temporarily revert the batch-timeout tweak in Canary while we triage? Pros: reduces noise. Cons: loses latency win.

Random scribbles / heuristics that helped during triage:
- If repetition correlates strongly with token length of prompt > 350 tokens, likely KV-flush boundary.
- For factual snippets, force a 2-step verification prompt (ask model to list sources then answer) as a quick internal guardrail to catch invented dates.

Short TODOs (checkboxes):
- [ ] Run deterministic higher-n replicate for S1/S8 (due 2024-11-05)
- [ ] Add KV flush microtest (owner: Leo)
- [ ] Add tracing flags on Canary (owner: Aria)
- [ ] Draft quick Slack note to @infra describing suspected prefetch/attention interaction

End-of-shift note: prioritize low-effort, high-visibility mitigations (tracing + focused microtests) over immediate rollback. Capture reproducible sample and escalate if >10% regression at scale.

PRN: will convert clean samples to a small Confluence page if triage yields a concrete repro.
